title: Dedicated capacity: Smart Hedge & Release policy for burstable reservations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
background: Large customers reserve capacity for predictable throughput. We frequently observe transient demand spikes where reserved pools sit below utilization while adjacent reserved pools or opportunistic capacity have headroom. Current behavior either rejects burst traffic (hurting availability) or allows opaque cross-tenant borrowing via emergency backfill, leading to confusing billing and possible SLA violations. Customers ask for predictable burst behavior, transparent headroom borrowing, and clear failure modes.
goals:
1) Allow tenants to safely borrow short-term headroom (hedge) from a controlled pool with repayment semantics.
2) Provide transparent telemetry and billing signals for hedged usage and automated release windows.
3) Ensure bursts degrade gracefully via preemptive eviction policies and fallback model routing when hedging fails.
4) Offer operator-facing controls to set hedge budgets, release schedules, and preemption sensitivity per tenant.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in 5xx errors during spike events for reserved customers by >= 70% when hedging is enabled.
- Median P50 tail latency for hedged requests within 1.25x of baseline.
- Accurate hedged usage telemetry surfaced in Console for 95% of hedging windows.
- No increase in cross-tenant SLA violations attributable to hedging after 30d of rollout.
user_personas:
- Platform Product Managers (procurement/billing visibility)
- SRE/Oncall (incident handling, preemption observability)
- Tenant engineering teams (application owners needing predictable burst)
- Account managers/CS (negotiating reserve terms)
requirements_functional:
1) Hedge pool: a configurable sandboxed pool that can satisfy short bursts for eligible reserved tenants.
2) Hedge policy per tenant: headroom budget (tokens/minute), max concurrent hedged requests, repayment window (minutes/hours), and allowed preemption tolerance.
3) Transparent ledger: record hedged tokens, repayment events, and billing labels surfaced in Console and usage API.
4) Release windows: automatic release attempts at configured cadence; manual release button for operators.
5) Preemptive eviction: signal + graceful fallback (auto-route to hosted fallback model or queue) when hedged resources are reclaimed.
6) Audit & logs: every hedge allocation and eviction must be auditable with tenant id, reservation id, timestamp, and actor.
7) Operator controls: enable/disable hedging per reservation, adjust budgets, force repayments, and emergency drain.
8) Integration: billing system must tag hedged usage to separate line-item code.
9) Opt-in rule: hedging is off by default; tenant requests opt-in via API or console agreement.
10) Safety checks: global circuit breaker to stop hedging if hedge pool utilization exceeds threshold or cross-tenant contention spikes.
requirements_nonfunctional:
- Hedge allocation decision in <= 10ms in the request path.
- Telemetry latency: hedged-usage metrics should appear in Console within 90s.
- Preemption graceful window: clients must receive a preemption notice with at least 250ms of notice for in-flight streaming requests when possible.
- Security: all hedge operations must be logged and encrypted in transit; KMS integration required for audit exports.
- Scalability: design to support 10k concurrent hedged flows across clusters at GA.
ui_notes:
- Console: Reservation detail page adds a 'Hedging' card (current budget used, recent hedged windows, chart of hedged tokens).
- Action: 'Request Hedge' toggle in reservation config with slider for budget and repayment window.
- Alerts: automated alert templates for customers when hedge usage > 80% of budget.
- Audit view: sortable table with hedging events, filters by tenant, reservation, date range.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha, 2 weeks): implement hedge pool + simple per-tenant policy; enable for internal teams.
Phase 2 (beta, 6 weeks): expose console controls, telemetry, and billing tags; onboard 3 pilot customers.
Phase 3 (GA, 4 weeks): finalize RBAC, KMS audit export, and operator controls; open opt-in to all reserved tenants.
Fallback plan: if hedging causes cross-tenant SLA degradation in beta, disable hedging for offending zones and extend repayment windows while iterating policy thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hedge pool exists and can be configured in infra (ENG validation).
- Per-tenant policy applied and enforceable: tests show hedged request counts respect budget and concurrency.
- Telemetry: Console surfaces hedged usage chart and ledger entries for sample tenants.
- Billing: hedged usage shows separate line-items in test billing export.
- Preemption: simulated eviction sends preemption notifications and triggers fallback routing in 95% of test cases.
- Security: audit logs for hedging events are present and exportable via KMS to external SIEM.
- Operator controls: toggle off/on and force-drain actions succeed and are logged.
- Documentation: PRD, runbook, and quickstart for customers drafted and reviewed by SRE, Security, and Billing teams.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Hedging could be used as a loophole to bypass reserved limits -> Mitigation: strict opt-in, billing differentiation, and rate-limited hedging budgets.
- Risk: Preemption could cause user-visible quality regressions -> Mitigation: require graceful fallback routes and conservatively sized hedging budgets in early rollout.
- Risk: Telemetry lag hides overuse -> Mitigation: add immediate event logging to both metrics pipeline and Console with fallback to raw logs.
- Risk: Complex billing disputes -> Mitigation: include clear ledger exports and reconciliation docs; surface human-readable invoices with hedging breakdown.
open_questions:
- What is the right default repayment window for most tenants (30m, 1h, 4h)?
- Should hedging budgets be convertible to monetary credits for automatic chargebacks?
- How to express hedged usage in SLA contracts (is hedged traffic counted against reserved SLA)?
- Do we allow cross-zone hedging or limit to same AZ for data locality reasons?
- Can we expose a simulation API so tenants can run 'what-if' forecasts for hedging?
